SMTO-CMP-0033 — The AI checked for a value that its steps never recorded

GUID: 22cf1edb-d6da-49cc-85f8-b8bf3fa9bfff
Slug: completion-unobserved-check-value
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • To prove the task worked, the AI pointed to a value in a step's output, but that value isn't there. SMTO won't accept a value that was never actually seen, so it asked the AI to look again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task still shows Running, wait. SMTO has asked the AI to read the value it needs before claiming it. Only a real reading shows whether the value is what the task needs.
  2. If the task stops as Partial · resumable, expand the task and open the steps to see what their output actually contains. You can see whether the value exists at all, or whether the AI looked in the wrong place.
  3. Send a message asking SMTO to check the current state and report the actual value. Only ask for a change if that value is wrong. This confirms the result without repeating a change that may already be in place.

What success looks like

  • The AI reports a value that appears in a step's output, and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't make the change again just because the value wasn't found.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A completion check's JSON pointer could not be resolved or interpreted in the cited receipt's stored data, so the asserted value was never observed.

What this means

  • JSON-pointer resolution cannot find or interpret the requested check value in retained receipt data. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • JSON-pointer resolution cannot find or interpret the requested check value in retained receipt data.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact operation receipt and pointer; do not invent the missing value or use a nearby field.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cited operation's receipt data and the check's pointer from completion_feedback. Observe the required value with an operation that actually returns it and point the check at that field; never invent the value or substitute a nearby field.
  • Observe the required check value before asserting it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported observation contains the actual required value at the cited location.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
